title: Fats's own big-band writing; Kirkeby 'eases in'
summary: Fats wrote 'Beefsteak Serenade' and 'Come and Get It' for the big band's 12-inch recordings, while Kirkeby, hired to handle business, looked after his own.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Did Fats write any of the arrangements for the big band?
Yes. "Beefsteak Serenade -- Serenade", "Come and Get It," I cant think right off now, but the big band, that's the --
But he did write quite a few-- (inaudible).
-- big -- what do you call it, 12-inch, I think it was, we did. Yeah, uh-huh. More or less. Yeah. Okay, when we recorded with the big band, 12-inch. And he
did most of them, and of course we had another -- (laughs). Another country was -- Mr. Kirkeby eased in there, you know. (Laughter.)
Well, how do you mean he eased in there? Was he --
Well, at that time he was managing things for Fats. He wasn't managing Fats. Fats hired him to take care of his business for him. That's the way that -- (laughs). And he took care! (Laughter.)
